verdict.rationale: pnpm documents per-project pinning of Node.js (via devEngines.runtime, installed by pnpm itself) and automatic switching to the pnpm version declared in package.json on first use. That covers the tool-version half of the story when pnpm commands run, though not as a shell-level activation on directory entry. Nothing shows pnpm loading or activating project environment variables; ${NAME} substitution only reads existing variables into config files. missing for 10: automatic activation on cd/directory entry, per-project environment variable loading, support for tools beyond Node.js/pnpm, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the right tool versions and environment variables activate automatically when I enter a project directory

citations.quote: Install and pin Node.js per project straight from pnpm — no nvm, no shell hooks, no “works on my machine” version mismatches.
If your `package.json` has a `packageManager` or `devEngines.packageManager` field, pnpm switches to that version on first use
Works as a Node.js version manager.
